In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of chlorophyll photobleaching in relation to the effects of heat stress on the organisation of the chloroplast thylakoid membrane.
the effects of heat stress on the photosynthetic electron transport system in pea leaves and isolated chloroplasts.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of heat stress damage in photosynthetic membranes and with the identification of the factors that contribute to the recovery of heat-stressed plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increased susceptibility of PSI to photooxidation in heat-stressed chloroplats is due to the inhibition of PS II activity.

the increased susceptibility of chloroplasts to photobleaching under heat stress is due to a change in the organisation of PSI and that this change is a direct consequence of the interruption of the reductant supply from PSII to the PSI reaction centre.

the major effect of high temperature on the photosynthetic activity of pea chloroplasts is a severe disruption in the organisation of photosystem II and the consequent inhibition of the supply of reducing power for the photosynthetic electron transport chain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heat-stressed chloroplastic membranes become increasingly leaky to protons.

the photosynthetic machinery of pea chloroplasts becomes progressively disrupted at temperatures between 45 and 55°C, and that the first sign of damage occurs in the organisation of PSII, followed by a disruption of electron transport from PSII to the PSI reaction centre.
heat stress leads to the formation of a photosynthetic apparatus with a reduced efficiency of energy conversion and with a reduced capacity to protect itself against photobleaching.
The main takeaway from our work is that

heat stress causes the formation of a new, highly reactive, chlorophyll-containing species, which is formed in a temperature range where the activity of the photosynthesizing apparatus is severely affected.
heat stress can lead to a major rearrangement of the photosynthesising apparatus in the chloroplasts of higher plants.

the heat-induced changes in the organisation and activity of the photosyntheic apparatus of heat-stress pea chloroplasts are such that they lead to a greatly enhanced susceptibility of PSI to photooxidation.
